sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. Set TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType to AUTO (early_stopping_type='Auto' in the SDK); after each epoch the job's objective metric is compared with the median of running averages of previous jobs at the same epoch and stopped if worse; 'To support early stopping, an algorithm must emit objective metrics for each epoch'; for PyTorch 'you must write code that computes the objective metric and logs it after each epoch'.

brief.situation: You are the ML engineer at Ferrow Logistics. A SageMaker AI hyperparameter tuning job for the delivery-time model runs 60 training jobs of 50 epochs each on GPU instances, with early stopping set to Auto. Half the jobs are done, every one ran all 50 epochs, and the month's GPU budget is 70% spent. Finance freezes GPU spend at 18:00 if the forecast exceeds the budget.
handover: The training script is custom PyTorch in script mode; it prints the validation MAE once, at the end.
The tuning objective metric is validation:mae, minimized, parsed from the logs with a regex.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the tuning job, its training jobs, the objective metric they report and the early-stopping decision.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why early stopping never fired, what you changed, and how the next tuning job stays in budget.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Early stopping was Auto, but train.py printed validation MAE once after the loop; the tuner compares each job's objective after every epoch with earlier jobs, so with one datapoint it never stopped anything.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: train.py logs validation MAE every epoch; the remaining trials run as a warm-start tuning job with early stopping, and 12 of 18 weak jobs stopped early. Stopping and deploying the best-so-far skips half the search; fewer epochs keeps the same problem.

parts.label: Budget
parts.modelAnswer: The training template tests for per-epoch metrics, and a budget action pauses new tuning jobs at 85%.

halfModel.headline: Make early stopping work; do not abandon the search
halfModel.body: Early stopping saves budget only if jobs report the objective every epoch. Fix the reporting and let the tuner stop weak jobs.

gpuFrozen.headline: Early stopping needs a metric per epoch
gpuFrozen.body: The tuner compares each job's objective after every epoch; a script that reports once gives it nothing to compare.

scoring.modelReasoning: Early stopping is on, yet no job stopped, and each job has a single objective datapoint: the script prints validation MAE only after training. The tuner can only stop a job by comparing its metric after each epoch, so log the metric every epoch and resume the remaining trials as a warm-start tuning job, then check that weak jobs stop and the forecast falls. Deploying the best-so-far abandons half the search; fewer epochs keeps the same blind spot.
